The subject demographics table every ADaM deliverable carries: age and its groups, sex
and race, summarised by treatment arm, built from `pharmadata.pharmaverseadam.adsl` in
polars. It copies the target table of the
[R demographic table example](https://pharmaverse.github.io/examples/tlg/demographic.html),
which does the same with {cards} and {gtsummary}.

The blocks run as the page is rendered, and the table is printed by the code rather than
written into the page.

::: {#77b86ab3 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import polars as pl

from pharmadata import pharmaverseadam as adam
```
:::


## The population

The analysis population is the 254 subjects who were randomised and treated; screen
failures stay out of the table. The two recodes are display spellings only.

::: {#b3991413 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
ARMS = ["Placebo", "Xanomeline High Dose", "Xanomeline Low Dose"]

adsl = adam.adsl.filter(pl.col("ACTARM") != "Screen Failure").with_columns(
    pl.col("SEX").replace_strict({"M": "MALE", "F": "FEMALE"}),
    pl.when(pl.col("AGE").is_between(18, 40))
    .then(pl.lit("18-40"))
    .when(pl.col("AGE").is_between(41, 64))
    .then(pl.lit("41-64"))
    .when(pl.col("AGE") > 64)
    .then(pl.lit(">=65"))
    .alias("AGEGR1"),
)
```
:::


## Statistics as rows

A long frame worn as a wide one: one row per statistic, per arm. Two functions produce
those rows, one for a numeric variable and one for a categorical, and a third names a
block.

::: {#589e9712 .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
def group(label: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """The bold row that opens a block of characteristics."""
    return pl.DataFrame({"ACTARM": [""], "label": [f"**{label}**"], "value": [""]})


def one_decimal(column: str) -> pl.Expr:
    return pl.col(column).round(1).cast(pl.String)


def summarise(df: pl.DataFrame, variable: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """N, Mean (SD), Median (Q1, Q3) and Min, Max of one numeric variable, by arm."""
    return (
        df.group_by("ACTARM", maintain_order=True)
        .agg(
            pl.col(variable).count().alias("N"),
            pl.col(variable).mean().alias("mean"),
            pl.col(variable).std().alias("sd"),
            pl.col(variable).median().alias("median"),
            pl.col(variable).quantile(0.25, interpolation="linear").alias("q1"),
            pl.col(variable).quantile(0.75, interpolation="linear").alias("q3"),
            pl.col(variable).min().alias("low"),
            pl.col(variable).max().alias("high"),
        )
        .select(
            "ACTARM",
            pl.col("N").cast(pl.String),
            pl.concat_str(
                [one_decimal("mean"), pl.lit(" ("), one_decimal("sd"), pl.lit(")")]
            ).alias("Mean (SD)"),
            pl.concat_str(
                [
                    one_decimal("median"),
                    pl.lit(" ("),
                    one_decimal("q1"),
                    pl.lit(", "),
                    one_decimal("q3"),
                    pl.lit(")"),
                ]
            ).alias("Median (Q1, Q3)"),
            pl.concat_str(
                [one_decimal("low"), pl.lit(", "), one_decimal("high")]
            ).alias("Min, Max"),
        )
        .unpivot(index="ACTARM", variable_name="label", value_name="value")
    )
```
:::


The `unpivot` turns the four formatted statistics into four rows. A name given with
`alias()` becomes the row's label, so the display strings are built before it.

::: {#d003e532 .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
def counts(df: pl.DataFrame, variable: str, levels: list[str]) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """n (%) at each level of one categorical variable, by arm."""
    return (
        pl.DataFrame({"ACTARM": ARMS})
        .join(pl.DataFrame({variable: levels}), how="cross")
        .join(
            df.group_by("ACTARM", variable).len(name="n"),
            on=["ACTARM", variable],
            how="left",
        )
        .with_columns(pl.col("n").fill_null(0))
        .join(df.group_by("ACTARM").len(name="N"), on="ACTARM")
        .select(
            "ACTARM",
            pl.col(variable).alias("label"),
            pl.concat_str(
                [
                    pl.col("n").cast(pl.String),
                    pl.lit(" ("),
                    (100 * pl.col("n") / pl.col("N")).round(1).cast(pl.String),
                    pl.lit("%)"),
                ]
            ).alias("value"),
        )
    )
```
:::


The cross join is the point of that first line. No subject is between 18 and 40, so a
`group_by` would drop the level silently; the levels are part of the specification, so
they are listed and counts are joined onto them.

## Assemble, then pivot

::: {#43eb6553 .cell execution_count=5}
``` {.python .cell-code}
long = pl.concat(
    [
        group("Age (yr)"),
        summarise(adsl, "AGE"),
        group("Age group"),
        counts(adsl, "AGEGR1", ["18-40", "41-64", ">=65"]),
        group("Sex"),
        counts(adsl, "SEX", ["FEMALE", "MALE"]),
        group("Race"),
        counts(
            adsl,
            "RACE",
            ["AMERICAN INDIAN OR ALASKA NATIVE", "BLACK OR AFRICAN AMERICAN", "WHITE"],
        ),
    ]
)
```
:::


`pivot()` puts an arm in each column. It does not promise a row order, so the order of
first appearance is captured before the pivot and joined back after it.

::: {#1e2ce50a .cell execution_count=6}
``` {.python .cell-code}
order = (
    long.get_column("label")
    .unique(maintain_order=True)
    .to_frame()
    .with_columns(pl.int_range(pl.len()).alias("ord"))
)

tlf = (
    long.pivot(index="label", on="ACTARM", values="value")
    .join(order, on="label")
    .sort("ord")
    .drop("ord")
    .rename({"label": "Characteristic"})
    .select("Characteristic", *ARMS)
)
```
:::


## The table

polars' `_repr_html_` escapes the markdown in the group-row labels, so the page builds a
markdown table by hand and hands it to Quarto with `IPython.display.Markdown`, which
renders it as an HTML table and keeps the bold group headers intact.

::: {#bc2507b7 .cell execution_count=7}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from IPython.display import Markdown, display


def to_markdown(df: pl.DataFrame) -> str:
    """Render a frame as a markdown table."""
    lines = [
        "| " + " | ".join(df.columns) + " |",
        "| " + " | ".join(["---"] * df.width) + " |",
    ]
    for row in df.iter_rows():
        cells = ["" if value is None else str(value) for value in row]
        lines.append("| " + " | ".join(cells) + " |")
    return "\n".join(lines)


display(Markdown(to_markdown(tlf)))
```

## Two things the numbers depend on

**A quartile is a definition, not a value.** polars' `quantile()` defaults to
`interpolation="nearest"`, which answers with an observed age: on the high-dose arm it
puts Q1 at 71.0. `linear` is the definition numpy, pandas and R's `quantile(type = 7)`
share, and it interpolates, giving 70.5. The R example prints 70.0, because R's own
default is `type = 2`, which averages the two observations instead of interpolating.

**Race has three levels here, not four.** ADSL holds two screen-failure subjects
recorded ASIAN, so this population has none. Dropping the population filter is one
line, and the fourth level appears with it.
